purpose: Teach: いらいら/ぬれ/よかろ/しょせん/近ごろ/ぎみ/おもむろに/あやしい

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはいらいらせずに、待っていらしたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father—he never got impatient. He just waited.
lines.style: Slow, measured opening. Voice drops slightly, reaching back into memory. Gentle certainty, like holding something precious that's already gone. Slight pause before 'waited'—letting it settle.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、雨の日に上着がぬれてもへっちゃらでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes—and your father, dear, he didn't mind when his coat got soaked in the rain, did he?
lines.style: Warm, affectionate clarity. Nodding as she speaks. A small laugh underneath—the delight of shared memory. Leans slightly toward him on 'did he'—that familiar check-in, almost rhetorical.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「家族が元気ならよかろう」と仰ったぞ
lines.en: Gran, back then, your father used to say, 'If the family's well, that's all that matters.'
lines.style: Quotes gently, not performing the words—just offering them up as fact. Voice steadies around the remembered phrase. A hum of quiet conviction underneath. Eyes distant.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様も「しょせん人生は一度」と仰ってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your grandson, dear—he used to say 'Life happens only once,' didn't he?
lines.style: Bright recognition in the voice. Slight tilt upward on 'grandson'—pride and a touch of mischief. The question at the end is intimate, not searching. She's asking him to remember with her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、近ごろ、お孫様の顔を見られて嬉しかったぞ
lines.en: Gran, lately… I've been so glad to see our grandson's face.
lines.style: Voice catches almost imperceptibly on 'lately.' Opens with warmth but held tightly. Slower pace. The emotion is real but kept contained—only the eyes would betray it. Trailing soft.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、いつも元気でも疲れぎみでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandson, dear—he always seemed well, but a little weary underneath, didn't he?
lines.style: Gentler register now. Observant, almost maternal concern. Not questioning—stating what she's noticed and inviting him to see it too. Soft but clear.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがおもむろに刀を磨かれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father would quietly polish his sword.
lines.style: Ceremonial quiet. Each word distinct, patient. The image settles—no rush. Voice hollows slightly with the weight of what that meant. Respectful, almost ritualistic.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、夜中にあやしい影を見たって仰ってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you used to tell me you'd seen strange shadows at night, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Voice softens further, almost whispered. A small smile—she's protective of this memory. The question is gentle, not probing. Trailing very softly on the final words, like the memory itself is drifting away.
